issues.description: The problem statement/UML specifies a Stock method emptyStock(): void, and the solution implements emptyStock(), but the template repository's Stock class provides a method named clearInventory() instead. This name/signature mismatch is structural: students following the template will not find emptyStock to call or implement, leading to confusion and potential test failures if exercises or tests expect emptyStock.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem specification and solution by renaming the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a public emptyStock() method that delegates to clearInventory(). Also update any references in the template/comments so the method name matches the UML and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template repository's Stock class defines a method named clearInventory() instead. This mismatch (emptyStock vs. clearInventory) refers to the same conceptual operation (clearing the stock) and may confuse students when mapping the UML/problem text to the provided starter code and the expected final implementation.
